arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/calculate_correlation.py
import math

# Belgian Franc Positions (millions) - From Table FCP-II-1 (Nonbanking Firms' Positions)
# Net position column, Worldwide rows
belgian_francs = [10164, 2245, 16408, 13327]  # Dec 1975, Mar 1976, Jun 1976, Sep 1976

# Canadian Dollar Positions (millions) - From Table FCP-III-1 (Nonbanking Firms' Positions)
# Net position column, Worldwide rows  
canadian_dollars = [10371, 10724, 11176, 10806]  # Dec 1975, Mar 1976, Jun 1976, Sep 1976

# Calculate means
n = len(belgian_francs)
x_mean = sum(belgian_francs) / n
y_mean = sum(canadian_dollars) / n

print(f"Belgian Francs: {belgian_francs}")
print(f"Canadian Dollars: {canadian_dollars}")
print(f"n = {n}")
print(f"x_mean = {x_mean}")
print(f"y_mean = {y_mean}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
numerator = sum((belgian_francs[i] - x_mean) * (canadian_dollars[i] - y_mean) for i in range(n))
print(f"\nNumerator: {numerator}")

sum_sq_x = sum((x - x_mean) ** 2 for x in belgian_francs)
sum_sq_y = sum((y - y_mean) ** 2 for y in canadian_dollars)
print(f"Sum of squared deviations (x): {sum_sq_x}")
print(f"Sum of squared deviations (y): {sum_sq_y}")

denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_x * sum_sq_y)
print(f"Denominator: {denominator}")

r = numerator / denominator
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r}")
print(f"Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(r, 4)}")
EOF
python3 /tmp/calculate_correlation.py
